messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Have stat_smooth use larger domain for calculations than displayed
parts:
Hi:

If I interpreted this correctly, all you should need to do is truncate
the lower end of the x-axis at x = 42218, which you can do with
coord_cartesian() or xlim(). I suppressed the vertical line; the
coord_cartesian() insert is just before the first call to theme(). I
set the lower end to 42217 to avoid partial cutoff of the points at
42218.

BTW, thanks for the intro to R-Fiddle; I hadn't seen it before.

Dennis

y = Popular_Support,
colour=Party,
size=1/Error,
weight=1/Error)) +
scale_size_area(guide="none", max_size=4) +
geom_point()+
stat_smooth(span = 1, , show_guide= F) +
# geom_vline(xintercept = 42216, linetype = 5, color='darkgray',show_guide= F)+
scale_colour_manual(values = c(Conservative="blue",
Liberal="red",
NDP="orange",
Green="green3",

geom_text(data=LastElection, show_guide=F, aes(label =
c(39.6,18.9,30.6,"6.0",3.9)), size=3.5, hjust=-.2, vjust=-0.4)+

Aug','15 Aug','20 Aug','25 Aug','30 Aug','4 Sep','9 Sep','14 Sep','19
Sep','24 Sep','29 Sep','4 Oct','9 Oct','14 Oct','19 Oct\nElection')) +

How do you do that when the data used to compute the stat_smooth()s is
taken from the polls data, whose date range is

> range(polls$Date)
[1] 42218 42237

Your last sentence does not make sense to me in that context. Are you
saying you want the data from May to be included in the smooths but
you only want the smooths to be visible after the cutoff date? If so,
you may have to use the coord_cartesian() idea as the first part of
the plot, and then add the vertical line and points to it afterward.
The training process should expand the time scale for you
automatically. I'd save the scaling and theming for the end.

Dennis
